findings.observation: Examined Sheet 1 (Cover) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) and all other plan sheets for Austin Energy contact information. Sheet 1 (Cover) contains contact information for City of Austin - Water and Wastewater Utility, Austin Water, and Austin Fire Department, but no Austin Energy contact block with phone numbers, addresses, or department names. Sheet 3 contains utility-related notes but no standalone contact information block for Austin Energy.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.16.0 requires current Austin Energy contact information to be shown on plan sheets to enable coordination. The absence of contact information (phone number, department name, address) means developers and contractors cannot readily reach Austin Energy for required coordination. The presence of contact information for other city departments (Water, Fire) but not Austin Energy constitutes a deficiency in providing this required information.
findings.comment: Current Austin Energy contact information (phone number and department name) is not provided on the cover sheet or plan sheets. Add a contact block with Austin Energy department phone number and current contact information for coordination purposes.

applicableAreas: Austin Energy Notes section on Sheet 3
findings.observation: Reviewed the complete 'Electric Notes' section on Sheet 3 (Blocks 8 and 14). The section contains five notes addressing tree pruning rights, easement access, erosion control and tree protection, clearance maintenance, and relocation costs. Vision analysis specifically searched for and confirmed the absence of any disclaimer stating that: (1) electric facilities shown are conceptual only, (2) plans should not be used for bidding purposes, or (3) final electric design by Austin Energy may vary from that shown. None of these three elements are present in the Electric Notes section.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.16.0 requires a disclaimer that establishes the preliminary/conceptual nature of electric service design and acknowledges that final design approval by Austin Energy may require changes. This disclaimer serves both informational and legal purposes, ensuring contractors understand the design is not final and may change. The absence of this disclaimer fails to communicate the conceptual nature of the shown design and that Austin Energy may require modifications.
findings.comment: Missing note stating that electric facilities shown are conceptual only, should not be used for bidding purposes, and that final electric design by Austin Energy may vary from that shown. Add a comprehensive disclaimer covering all three elements before the standard Austin Energy notes.

applicableAreas: Austin Energy Notes section on Sheet 3
findings.observation: Reviewed the complete 'Electric Notes' section (Blocks 8 and 14 on Sheet 3). The five notes address tree pruning, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and relocation costs. Vision analysis specifically searched for a note requiring coordination with Austin Energy when plans change. No note is present that lists specific change types triggering Austin Energy review, such as changes in: building square footage, building location, detention facilities location, grading, or spoil site locations.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.16.0 requires notification requirements when design changes occur. A coordination note ensures developers understand that modifications to the site plan—particularly those affecting grading, building location, or detention facilities—require Austin Energy review and approval before implementation. The absence of this note fails to establish the coordination pathway for inevitable plan changes during design development and construction.
findings.comment: Missing note stating that Austin Energy must review any changes to plans that may affect electric requirements, including changes to building square footage, building location, detention facilities location, grading, and spoil site locations. Add this coordination requirement as a distinct note in the Austin Energy Notes section.

findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 3 confirmed the exact wording of the section heading for the notes containing the five Austin Energy requirements. The heading reads exactly as 'Electric Notes', not 'Austin Energy Notes'. The sheet also contains a separate section headed 'Electric Transmission Notes' for transmission-specific requirements.
findings.reasoning: The General Site Plan Notes document specifies that notes must use the exact heading 'Austin Energy Notes'. The grouping guidance explicitly warns that variations such as 'Utility Notes', 'City of Austin Electric Notes', or 'Additional General Utility Notes' are non-compliant. The heading 'Electric Notes' is a variation that omits 'Austin Energy', creating ambiguity about which utility's requirements are being presented and potentially confusing contractors about which entity's standards apply.
findings.comment: The Austin Energy Notes section heading reads 'Electric Notes' instead of the required 'Austin Energy Notes'. Change the section heading to read exactly 'Austin Energy Notes'.

applicableAreas: Austin Energy Transmission Notes on Sheet 3
findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains 'Electric Transmission Notes' (Block 20) with 16 detailed notes addressing transmission easement requirements, clearances, pre-construction meetings, barricades, and construction coordination. Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) using vision analysis specifically searching for transmission infrastructure. Result: No transmission towers, transmission structures, transmission poles, or transmission easement labels are shown on the site plan. The site shows only 5-foot distribution electric easements and standard overhead distribution lines (OHE notation). Facts.md confirms plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements (distribution voltage) but lists no transmission easements or transmission structures on the property.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.14.0 defines transmission facilities as operating at 60kV phase-to-phase or higher and establishes that transmission-specific requirements apply only 'when transmission infrastructure is involved' or when development is within 100 feet of transmission line wires. The site plan shows no transmission infrastructure, transmission structures, or transmission easements. Including detailed transmission notes (addressing 48-hour pre-construction meetings, transmission easement road requirements, 25-foot clearance zones, and OSHA transmission safety) when no transmission infrastructure is shown or present on the plans constitutes inclusion of inapplicable notes.
findings.comment: Electric Transmission Notes are included on Sheet 3 (Block 20), but no transmission infrastructure, transmission structures, or transmission easements are shown on the site plan. Remove the 16 Electric Transmission Notes, or provide evidence of transmission infrastructure presence. If transmission facilities are located adjacent to the property, obtain and reference a specific Austin Energy coordination letter confirming transmission proximity and the applicability of these notes.

applicableAreas: Austin Energy Notes section on Sheet 3
findings.observation: Transcribed the complete text of the four Electric Notes on Sheet 3 (Blocks 8 and 14) and compared each against the standard four notes specified in the grouping's Regulatory Overview section. All four required notes are present, but each contains material modifications and additions beyond the standard text: Note 1 adds 'Austin Energy will perform all tree work in compliance with Chapter 25-8, Subchapter B...'; Note 2 changes 'shall' to 'of this subdivision/lot shall' and adds a full sentence about Chapter 25-8 compliance and easement location; Note 3 replaces 'proposed overhead electrical facilities' with 'proposed overhead electric facilities designed to provide electric service to this project' and adds 'The owner shall include Austin Energy's work within the limits of construction for this project'; Note 4 changes 'owner' to 'owner of the property' and adds two sentences about rendering electric service and cost responsibility.
findings.reasoning: The General Site Plan Notes document preface states: 'Changing the required text in your plan set will result in rejection of the application.' The grouping reinforces this requirement, stating 'Notes must use the exact wording provided in the current General Site Plan Notes document.' The four notes on Sheet 3, while addressing the correct topics, have been substantively modified with additional clauses, different word order, and supplementary text. These modifications constitute non-standard wording that deviates from the required standard text.
findings.comment: The four Electric Notes on Sheet 3 contain non-standard wording with additions and modifications to the required text. Replace all four notes with the exact text from the current General Site Plan Notes document. The General Site Plan Notes document preface states that changing the required text will result in application rejection.

findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 3 identified the 'Electric Notes' section heading (Block 8) containing five numbered notes, followed by a spatial break and an unheaded duplicate block of text (Block 14) immediately below the 'Fire Department' notes section. The unheaded block contains the exact same five notes verbatim: 'Austin Energy has the right to prune...', through 'Any relocation of electric facilities...'. The two blocks are located in different positions on the same sheet, creating visual duplication of the entire set of Electric Notes.
findings.reasoning: The General Site Plan Notes document and standard practice require a single, unified Austin Energy Notes section on the site plan. Duplicate sections create confusion about which set of notes is authoritative, may lead contractors to overlook critical requirements by assuming they appear elsewhere, and violate the principle that each set of standard notes should appear once per sheet. This duplication represents poor organization and potential non-compliance with City standards requiring a single cohesive notes section.
findings.comment: The Electric Notes section (five notes) appears twice on Sheet 3—once as the labeled 'Electric Notes' section (Block 8) and again as an unheaded duplicate block below the Fire Department notes (Block 14). Remove the duplicate unheaded block and retain only the single labeled 'Electric Notes' section.

applicableAreas: Sheet 3 Austin Energy Notes and Sheet 21 Electrical Design Plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly depicts underground electrical service with labeled 'Underground Electric Line' routing throughout the site, including transformer pads, pull boxes, electrical meters, and connections to eight buildings. This represents developer-designed and (presumably) developer-installed underground electrical infrastructure/conduit. Reviewed Sheet 3 Electric Notes (Blocks 8 and 14) and Sheet 21 Utility Notes (Block 6): Sheet 3 contains five notes but none address developer responsibility for conduit installation or infrastructure meeting Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. Sheet 21 Utility Notes specify only contractor verification requirements for existing utilities and private water/wastewater branch materials, with no mention of electrical conduit or developer responsibility for meeting electrical design standards.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.3.0 establishes developer responsibilities when underground electric service is being designed and installed. When a site plan shows developer-designed underground electrical infrastructure (as evidenced by the blue Underground Electric Line routing on Sheet 21), a note must be present establishing that the developer is responsible for designing and constructing conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards, including conductor installation costs if applicable. The absence of this note leaves unclear who is responsible for the infrastructure shown and fails to establish that the design must comply with current (not outdated) Austin Energy standards.
findings.comment: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric service lines and associated infrastructure designed for the project, but no note on either Sheet 3 or Sheet 21 establishes developer responsibility for conduit and related infrastructure or requires compliance with current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. Add a note stating: 'Developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy (AE) Design Criteria Manual, including the installation of conductors if determined during the design process (prior to the issuance of the building permit) that the developer will fund the installation cost of the conductors. The Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve all conflicts. All costs associated with these improvements will be the responsibility of the applicant.'
